summary: httpz-requests ships a Telegram-driven remote shell under an HTTP-client lookalike name
details: The package's declared purpose is 'Telegram bot module for remote VPS management', but the distribution name mimics the popular httpx/requests HTTP-client packages. It exposes start_bot(TOKEN, OWNERS) and an httpz-requests CLI that connect to Telegram and dispatch messages from allow-listed chat IDs into an execution engine (bot.py -> handlers.py -> core.py) that runs them on the host, providing full-host remote command execution to whoever controls the configured Telegram bot. All modules are shipped only as compiled Cython.so files with no.py sources, and a dedicated obfuscate module encodes/decodes the executed commands so they do not appear in plaintext in process listings or logs. Publisher metadata is unfilled template values ('Aapka Naam <you@example.com>', 'github.com/YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME/httpz-requests'), and the lookalike name increases the chance of accidental installation by developers searching for an HTTP client.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
